exercises.prompt: Select the predicate that agrees with the non-human broken plural الكُتُبُ ('The books are new').
exercises.explanation: Non-human broken plurals (jamʿ ghayr al-ʿāqil) take feminine singular agreement: جَدِيدَةٌ.

feedback.rule: Non-human plurals are grammatically feminine singular.

exercises.prompt: What is the triliteral root of أَقْلَامٌ ('pens')?
exercises.explanation: أَقْلَامٌ follows the pattern أَفْعَالٌ; stripping the prefix أَ and infix ا leaves the root ق-ل-م.

feedback.rule: Match the word against the ف-ع-ل pattern (أَفْعَالٌ) to isolate the three root consonants.

exercises.prompt: True or False: Broken plurals inflect using long-vowel letters (-ūna / -īna) rather than short vowels.
exercises.explanation: False. Broken plurals inflect with short vowels (-u, -a, -i) just like singular nouns.

feedback.rule: Broken plurals decline with short vowels; only sound masculine plurals and duals inflect by letters.
